items.title: Law Commission of India to organise National Conference on ‘Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms: National and State Perspectives’
items.summary: Radhakrishnan, will inaugurate the Conference, in the presence of Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law & Justice. The senior leadership of the 23rd Law Commission of India—Chairperson, Justice (Retd.) Dinesh Maheshwari; Member, Prof. D.P. Verma; and Member Secretary, Dr. Anju Rathi Rana—will also be present.

facts.text: Radhakrishnan, will inaugurate the Conference, in the presence of Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law & Justice.

The Conference will deliberate on contemporary issues relating to law reforms, co-operative federalism, constitutional governance and institutional frameworks for the effective administration of justice.

The Conference will consider how the Union and the States can work together on legal reform within this constitutional framework, and how coordination between the Law Commission of India, State Law Commissions and equivalent bodies can be strengthened.

The first technical session, “Reforms in Law: Needs and Methods”, will examine the need for continuous review and reform of laws in response to social, economic and technological change, as well as the methods and institutional processes through which such reform may be undertaken.

items.title: PROVISIONAL INDEX OF CORE INDUSTRIES FOR THE MONTH OF SEPTEMBER 2026, AND FINAL INDEX FOR THE MONTH OF AUGUST 2026 WITH BASE YEAR 2022-23
items.summary: 21 OCT 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi Provisional Index of Core Industries for the month of September 2026 (Base Year 2022-23) Key highlights of ICI for the month of September 2026 The Index of Core Industries (ICI) grew by 7.9 per cent in September 2026 (Provisional) on a year-on-year basis, compared with September 2025 , higher than the growth rate of 5.9 per cent recorded in August 2026 (Final).

facts.text: 21 OCT 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi Provisional Index of Core Industries for the month of September 2026 (Base Year 2022-23) Key highlights of ICI for the month of September 2026 The Index of Core Industries (ICI) grew by 7.9 per cent in September 2026 (Provisional) on a year-on-year basis, compared …

Iron Ore, Electricity, Coal, Refinery Products, Cement, and Steel observed (Y-o-Y) growth rate of 18.4 per cent, 11.4 per cent, 10.7 per cent, 10.3 per cent, 9.8 per cent, and 4.9 per cent respectively, whereas Fertilizers, Natural Gas, and Crude Oil witnessed negative growth in September 2026.
Cumulative growth rate of ICI during April-September 2026 was 5.1 per cent (Provisional) compared to 2.5 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year.

items.title: India and New Zealand sign Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) on Electronic Origin Data Exchange to Facilitate Bilateral Trade Under the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA)
items.summary: India-New Zealand MoC will deepen Customs cooperation and support effective implementation of trade facilitation measures 21 OCT 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), India, and the New Zealand Customs Service (NZCS) signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) concerning Electronic Origin Data Exchange of Trade in Goods.

facts.text: India-New Zealand MoC will deepen Customs cooperation and support effective implementation of trade facilitation measures 21 OCT 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), India, and the New Zealand Customs Service (NZCS) signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (M…
The MoC was signed under the India-New Zealand FTA which entered into force from 20 th October, 2026.
The MoC was signed on 19 th October 2026 by Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC, and Ms. Christine Stevenson, Comptroller and Chief Executive, New Zealand Customs Service.

Importantly, the arrangement will support the effective utilisation of trade preferences under the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and help ensure that the benefits negotiated under the Agreement reach eligible businesses in both countries more efficiently and with greater certainty.
